newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ cuts business, home loan rates.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ cuts business, home loan rates.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Thursday it has cut its reference (prime) lending rate and home loan rates following a 0.5 percentage point fall in the official cash rate.
ANZ said its retail index rate and reference interest rate would both be cut 0.5 percentage points from August 29 to 8.75 percent and 8.45 percent respectively.
The bank said it would cut the variable interest rate on its basic home loan -- the ANZ Money Saver home loan -- by 0.61 points to 5.99 percent.
"ANZ is determined to be a very competitive provider of residential finance in today's market," said chief general manager Australian retail division Peter Hawkins.
ANZ said its standard variable home loan rate would fall to 6.70 percent from 6.99 percent. The changes would take effect from August 4 for new loans and September 15 for existing loans.
Australia's other three big banks cut rates on Wednesday after the Reserve Bank reduced the official cash rate.

Westpac Banking Corp reduced its standard variable mortgage rate by 0.51 points to 6.69 percent, the National Australia Bank Ltd cut its variable rate 0.50 points to 6.7 percent, and the Commonwealth Bank of Australia cut its standard rate 0.4 points to 6.8 percent.
